quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the right side of the lane.
Ride on the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain starts. Rain mixes with oil left by cars, making the surface slippery. Ride in tire tracks left by other cars to get better grip.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. What should you do?

options.text: You do not need to wear bright colors during the day.
You should wear bright colors during the day.
You should wear dark colors during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should wear bright colors during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear bright colors when riding to make yourself easier to see, even during the day.

questions.question: A good lane position should:

options.text: Make it harder for others to see you.
Give you at least one way to escape if danger appears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you at least one way to escape if danger appears.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed. Choose a position that gives you the most space around you.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Continue passing if you see an upcoming bridge.
Continue passing if you see an upcoming railroad crossing.
Try to pass more than one vehicle at once to save time.
Not follow another vehicle that is passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not follow another vehicle that is passing.
questions.explanation: Do not pass if it is not safe. Unsafe conditions include oncoming vehicles, pedestrians, bridges, curves, hills, intersections, or railroad crossings. Do not pass more than one vehicle at a time. Do not follow another vehicle that is already passing.

questions.question: When riding over grooved pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down to watch the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding through a work zone. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: How can you help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to help others see your motorcycle. Always check that your headlight works before you start riding.

questions.question: How can you reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change your BAC.

questions.question: During normal turns:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider lean in the same direction.
The motorcycle and rider lean in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider lean in the same direction.
questions.explanation: During a normal turn, the rider and motorcycle lean together at the same angle. During a slow, tight turn, the motorcycle leans while the rider keeps their body more upright.

questions.question: What insurance must you have to legally operate a motor vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Liability
questions.explanation: Your license can be suspended if you operate a motor vehicle without liability insurance.

questions.question: What separates traffic lanes moving in the same direction?
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect a rider's ability to ride safely?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride safely. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light to:

options.text: Tell other drivers you are riding near them.
Help other drivers see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
Warn other drivers you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light to warn other drivers when you slow down where they don't expect it. This is especially important when making tight, fast turns or slowing down on high-speed roads.

questions.question: If you are being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of the lane when being passed. Riding toward the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding away from it may cause the driver to cut back into your lane too early.

questions.question: When being passed, which part of the lane is safest for motorcyclists?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by an oncoming vehicle, stay in the center of your lane. Riding closer to the passing driver creates a hazard for both of you.

questions.question: How fast does the human body remove alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: About one drink per hour.
questions.explanation: The body removes about one drink per hour on average. This varies by person. Never ride after consuming any alcohol.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Ride at the same speed as daytime.
Ride slower than during the day.
Ride faster than during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night, especially on unfamiliar roads. Slower speed gives you more time to avoid hazards when visibility is low.

questions.question: Riding jackets and pants should:

options.text: Fit loose so wind can move the fabric.
Fit snug enough so they don't flap in the wind.
Fit tight so you cannot move freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snug enough so they don't flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly so they don't flap, but loose enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply controlled pressure to both front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum safe following distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Increase this distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: Experienced riders use SIPDE to make safe decisions. What does the "I" stand for?
questions.correctAnswerText: Identify
questions.explanation: SIPDE stands for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute. Experienced riders use this system to make safe decisions while riding.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: If another driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: You know they have seen you.
It does not always mean they have actually seen you.
They will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not always mean they have actually seen you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver has seen you just because they made eye contact. A driver may look at you and still not notice you.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: By the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. The rider uses their left foot to operate it.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, during a crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.
